content:
inc-bot: PAGER: gpu-pool-exhaustion detected in asia-northeast1 (page level: P1)
inc-bot: Symptoms: autoscaler pending (> 12m), request queue growth on runtime-prod, increased 5xx from serving (SLO breaches possible).

jordan: oncall here. seeing spike in queue length on runtime-prod. should be >1200 pending tasks, throughput flat. digging into autoscaler logs now.
sara: confirmed. autoscaler is hitting GCP GPU quota errors when attempting to create nodes. errors: 
```
ERROR: Compute: failed to create instance with accelerator: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded.
status: 403 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
project: redwood-prod-01 region: asia-northeast1
```

mike: can we failover to eu-west1 or spin up cpu fallback workers? how many customers impacted?
ana: (typo) ana: customer-impact: 12 active tenants on dedicated pools in that region, ~7k rps across batches, ephemeral hosted traffic also routed there. Trying to estimate user-facing errors now.
lucy: CS reporting increased error tickets from two enterprise customers in Japan — they see timeouts and inference failures.

jordan: mitigation plan attempt 1: apply short-term rate-limit to non-critical routes and lower concurrency for batch jobs to free GPU slots. rolling policy now: `rlimit non-essential 0.5` on runtime-prod.
sara: applying canary rate limit to /v1/generate/* for all free-tier keys. will monitor latency metrics.
mike: starting manual node creation to bypass autoscaler? hitting same quota error via gcloud.
```
gcloud compute instances create rwd-ephemeral-000 --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" --zone=asia-northeast1-b
```
-> returns same RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

ana: opened GCP support case: case ID CASE-2026-APAC-98765 with quota target increase request. Notified GCP SE. ETA unclear.
jordan: fallback attempt 2: re-route new traffic to eu-west1 and ap-southeast1 pools using smart-routing policy. Starting gradual diversion 5% -> 25% -> 50%. Executed route change: `policy set-route runtime-prod asia-northeast1->eu-west1 weight=+25`

sara: dashboards: 95th latency climbed from 320ms -> 1.6s. 5xx rate up from 0.3% -> 4.8% in last 8 minutes. Service error budget at risk.
mike: temporarily marking some reserved dedicated capacity as 'shared' to accept hosted traffic. This will affect isolation for 2 customers but reduces immediate SLO breach risk. pinging CS to notify them.
lucy: notified impacted customers about potential degraded performance + mitigation steps. they asked for ETA — told them 1-2 hours while we backfill capacity.

ana: update from GCP support-bot: "We've acknowledged CASE-2026-APAC-98765 and are reviewing. Quota increase requires org-level approval; may take 3-6 hours."

jordan: decision log: 1) divert traffic to eu-west1 immediate 2) enable CPU-fallback workers for small models for non-enterprise 3) reconfigure reserved->shared for 2 pools 4) escalate quota with GCP (done)
sara: executing CPU fallback for smaller models: `deploy runtime-prod-fallback --node-pool=cpu-fallback --selector=model.size<=small` — started. Expect lower quality for some prompts but prevents timeouts.
mike: rolling changes: closed some long-running batch jobs (job IDs: batch-3392, batch-3401) to free up queue. Also reduced worker concurrency on batch-queue to 2.

ana: customer-impact note for postmortem: - 12 tenants saw increased latencies, 3 tenants reported request failures, public API saw 5xx spike for ~18 minutes until failover stabilized.
jordan: oncall handoff: my shift ends in 45m. will prepare runbook and handoff to ana.

ana: taking over as next oncall. confirm current status: traffic diversion at 50% to eu-west1, CPU fallback active, reserved->shared applied, GCP case open. Is backend queue decreasing?
sara: queue trending down from 1200 -> 420 pending over 20m. 5xx rate down to 0.9%. 95th latency stabilizing ~480ms.
mike: manual cloud quota check: `gcloud compute regions describe asia-northeast1` shows GPUs used 98/100 (hard quota). Even if autoscaler requested 10 nodes, only 2 GPUs available. We hit org limit.

lucy: CS updated customers at 2026-06-03T06:45Z (internal). They acknowledged, want postmortem and timeline for quota resolution.

jordan: adding temporary runbook snippet for next shifts:
```
- If RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for GPUs in region: 1) divert traffic via policy (% steps) 2) enable cpu-fallback for non-enterprise routes 3) reduce batch concurrency 4) mark some reserved pools shared (only after notifying CS) 5) open GCP support case and escalate with account SE 6) if still failing, initiate cross-region full failover runbook
```

ana: leaving handoff note: 1) monitor case CASE-2026-APAC-98765, 2) hold on making further reserved->shared changes without PM approval, 3) keep CS looped.

jordan: re: post-incident followups: need to schedule quota pre-provisioning for peak hours, implement autoscaler logic to degrade model-size and prefer local smaller-vram models before scaling, and add proactive quota alarms.
sara: will add alerts: GPU-utilization-per-region > 90% for >5m -> page, configured. Also add check for autoscaler failures (quota errors) -> page.

gcp-support-bot: CASE-2026-APAC-98765 update: "We have increased quota by +50 GPUs in asia-northeast1 for project redwood-prod-01 (provisional). Changes will reflect within 45 minutes. Reference: INC-APAC-2026-987"

mike: confirming node creates now succeed. `gcloud compute instances create rwd-ephemeral-101 --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" --zone=asia-northeast1-b` -> success.
sara: autoscaler resumed scaling and pending queue drained to <50. 5xx back to baseline.

ana: closing incident thread for active mitigation. filing incident ticket and will follow up with postmortem. assigning actions: quota-preproc (sara), autoscaler-degrade-model (mike), reserved-pool-policy (kevin), customer-comms (lucy).
jordan: thanks all, good mitigation. handing off final notes to ana. :thumbsup:
ana: ack — taking postmortem ownership and will update timeline + action items in the incident tracker.
inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: gpu-pool-exhaustion asia-northeast1. Duration: 1h 10m.
